answer: Each identity grows its claim as a crystal, one layer per epoch, each layer built only from a verified job of that same epoch. A borrowed layer fractures the whole crystal. The crystal stands in a grove, a public stand, so each layer grows in sight. Any peer may hold a mirror to the crystal and recompute the lattice from the grove record without a jury: the reflection must match epoch for epoch, and one hollow layer — no job from its own epoch — drops the claim and forces regrowth. Ten crystals owe thirty epoch-bound layers no clone can share or backfill.
